critical_errors.coaching: One of your facts says data was stolen or copied. The logs show someone viewed the member portal, but nothing shows data leaving. Record that as a hypothesis or an unknown, and say what evidence would confirm it.

You recommended shutting everything down before working out what is affected. Shutting down hurts members and staff. Collect evidence, name the affected assets and set a severity first, then choose a response that matches.

response_scores.feedback: Best choice. Verifying with the employee and checking impact first avoids locking out the real person or tipping off an attacker, and protection follows straight after.
Reasonable, and it stops the access quickly. But acting before verifying could disrupt the real employee or miss the MFA change, so verify first when you can.
This stops access but is heavier than needed. Disabling the account blocks a real employee before you know the facts.
Waiting leaves a likely takeover in place. The evidence is strong enough to act on after verifying.
Far bigger than the problem. One account is involved, so shutting down all sign-ins and member services causes more harm than it prevents.

escalation_scores.feedback: The SOC lead is the right person to review a likely account takeover.
Escalating to the incident commander is reasonable because member data may have been viewed.
The help desk can help verify the employee, but it should not own a suspected takeover.
A suspected account takeover with member data involved should be escalated.

rationale: Two failed sign-ins followed by a success from a source this account never used is a classic sign of a guessed or reused password. It is an indicator, not proof.
A new MFA device requested a few minutes after the success suggests someone trying to keep access. It points to takeover, but it needs confirming.
The help-desk report that the employee did not sign in supports takeover. Confirm directly with the employee before acting.
Member data may have been viewed through the support portal. Whether any data left is unknown; say so instead of declaring it.
A proportionate response verifies identity and impact first, then resets the password, ends active sessions and reviews the MFA change.
